_tagGuide.spearhead: Flagship products we want to push. Anchors an order.
_tagGuide.general: Low-friction add-ons that lift AOV once a spearhead is in play.
_tagGuide.consumable: Gets used up — never excluded by ownership, people rebuy.
_tagGuide.accessory: Supporting gear. Not an anchor, not a general attach.
_tagGuide.NOTE: A product can carry several tags. PRO Mat is both `spearhead` (worth anchoring an order) and `general` (worth attaching when someone's buying a different spearhead). Anything already owned or in-cart is excluded, so a PRO Mat buyer is never pushed a PRO Mat.

_notes: RULE ORDER = PRIORITY. First match wins. Current order: cart-based AOV -> consumable upgrade -> spearhead attach -> specific accessory pairings.
`when` / `recommend` take product keys. `when_tags` / `recommend_tags` take tags. Mix freely.
`when_tags` = has ANY product with that tag. `when_not_tags` = has NO product with that tag (this is what makes the upgrade path work).
`when_scope: "cart"` matches only what's in the cart right now (abandoned-cart flows). Default matches cart + purchase history combined.
`{trigger}` in a reason is replaced with the product that fired the rule, e.g. 'Goes with your Digger Shield'.
Anything already owned or in the cart is excluded automatically - except `consumable` products, which people rebuy.
Fallback pushes spearheads: if we know nothing about someone, show them the flagship.
Regenerate mined data: npm run mine

EDGE CASES: `when_fleet: true` targets bulk buyers. `when_stale_tags` fires when a durable is older than edgeCases.durableOwnershipDays. Every decision carries a confidence score and telemetry — see scripts/diagnose.js.

durableOwnershipDays: after this long, a durable good stops counting as 'owned' — covers wear out in the Australian sun, so a 3-year-old cover is a replacement opportunity, not an exclusion. Consumables ignore this entirely.
fleetQuantityThreshold: total units in a single order at/above this = fleet buyer (Rental Ron, not Construction Charlie). Rules can target with when_fleet.
minConfidence: below this, the engine STOPS trusting itself and degrades to the safe fallback (spearheads) instead of showing a weak guess. A wrong rec in a fitment business costs a return.

freeShipping.label: free shipping
freeShipping._note: $399 Nudge Version (lib/nudge.js). Threshold moved 249 -> 399. Nudge picks the CHEAPEST relevant product that crosses the gap; overshooting the gap by more than maxOvershootMultiple is demoted so a $20 gap is never 'closed' with a $524 enclosure.
freeShipping._haulerFloor_note: Cart under this = a long way off the threshold, so the Hauler is force-included in the grid: at $399 it single-handedly clears $399 from any cart this size.

_sourceOfTruth: Shopify owns product FACTS (title, price, image, stock) via lib/catalog.js. This file owns STRATEGY only: key -> variant id, tags, rules, co-purchase, thresholds. `title` here is a HUMAN LABEL for reading this config and filling {trigger} in reason strings; the customer always sees the live Shopify title. `match` aliases are a FALLBACK for legacy order history that has no variant id -- new matching is by id, so a rename in Shopify can no longer silently break classification.

nonProducts._why: Line items that are NOT products: add-on services, insurance, tips, gift cards. They must never appear in a cart listing, never be recommended, and never count as 'unclassified' -- an unclassified line item halves recommendation confidence, so leaving Package Protection in dropped a perfect 1.0 match to 0.5. Shopify marks these UNLISTED (deliberately not storefront products); that status is not present in Klaviyo event data, so we match on variant id first, title second.

_displayOnly_note: displayOnly products exist so a range email can show them via /api/img?type=card. They carry no tags and are skipped by the nudge top-up pool, so adding one can never quietly change what the recommendation engine suggests.
